stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief, Harvey Jones chair

key_facts.fact: On November 11, 2026, Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, and appointed CFO Colette Kress, 59, as interim CEO while it searches for a successor; she keeps the CFO role.
key_facts.excerpt: On November 11, 2026, the Board of Directors ... accepted the resignation of Jen-Hsun Huang, as NVIDIA's President, Chief Executive Officer and member of the Board, effective immediately. ... the Board appointed NVIDIA's Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress, age 59, to serve as interim Chief Executive Officer

key_facts.fact: The board named Harvey C. Jones, a director since 1993 and former CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys, as Nvidia's first-ever board chair; the CEO search will consider internal and external candidates.
key_facts.excerpt: The Board of Directors appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever Chair of the Board ... including serving as Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of Synopsys. ... The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said it will still report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, November 17, at about 1:20 p.m. PT, as previously scheduled.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 17, at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT, as previously scheduled, followed by its earnings call at 2 p.m. PT.

key_facts.fact: The ouster followed a New York Times report on November 11 that Huang had a second extramarital affair, with Nvidia VP of Healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports to him, days after he admitted an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
key_facts.excerpt: The second alleged affair was with an executive who reports to him, Nvidia's vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, according to the Times.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported on November 11 that the board was preparing to oust Huang, and Bloomberg reported it had hired an outside firm to identify replacements; Semafor said some directors favored Kress as interim CEO and that Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji was under consideration.
key_facts.excerpt: Some members of Nvidia's board favor appointing Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO ... Nvidia has tapped an outside search firm to find the company's next CEO, Bloomberg reported. One person being considered for the top job is Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji

key_facts.fact: Nvidia shares were down nearly 12% in early trading on Thursday; since the previous Friday the stock had fallen as much as 19%, a market-cap loss of more than $855 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's shares were down nearly 12% in early morning trading on Thursday. Since Friday, the company's stock has fallen by as much as 19%, resulting in a market cap loss of more than $855 billion.

key_facts.fact: Rivals gained: AMD rose more than 4% pre-market after closing up 7.3%, and Broadcom gained 2.4% pre-market after a 4% gain, as the board weighed ousting Huang.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD's shares rose 4%+ pre-market, after closing up 7.3%, and Broadcom gained 2.4% pre-market, following a 4% gain, as Nvidia's board weighs ousting Jensen Huang

stories.headline: US finalizing rule to cut China's remote access to AI chips via data centers in seven countries

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on November 11 that the Commerce Department is finalizing a long-awaited rule to stop Chinese AI firms from remotely accessing advanced AI chips through data centers in other countries; it could be announced as soon as this month, and Commerce is consulting other agencies first.
key_facts.excerpt: The Commerce Department is preparing to finalize a rule that will prevent Chinese artificial intelligence companies from remotely accessing advanced AI chips through data centers located in other countries ... The rule could be announced this month ... The Commerce Department is consulting with other government agencies on the rule before it can be finalized

key_facts.fact: The rule would extend BIS controls to seven more countries (Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Brazil, Norway and South Africa), which would need Commerce approval to import Blackwell-class or more advanced Nvidia chips and report who uses them.
key_facts.excerpt: The additional targets are seven countries: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Brazil, Norway, and South Africa. ... those countries will need Commerce Department approval to import Nvidia's Blackwell-class and more advanced AI chips. Recipients must report who will receive the chips and how they will be used

key_facts.fact: US-run data centers in those countries would be exempt from licensing if they block remote access from arms-embargoed countries such as China and Russia and report customers' countries and compute scale.
key_facts.excerpt: data centers run by U.S. companies in those countries will be exempt from licensing if they meet certain conditions. Instead of allowing remote access from U.S. arms-embargoed countries such as China and Russia, operators must report customers' countries and the scale of computing.

key_facts.fact: Axios reported on November 11 that Trump approved action against suspected diversions of Nvidia chips to China three times this year (May, August and November 5), but Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler resisted; Commerce denied that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over Megaspeed.
key_facts.excerpt: On at least three separate occasions — in May, August, and Nov. 5 — Trump approved taking action against suspected diversions of Nvidia chips to China. But Lutnick and Commerce Undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler resisted pressure from Bessent and others to move forward. ... Commerce Department spokesperson Kristen Eichamer denied that Bessent confronted Lutnick

key_facts.fact: Commerce has not added a single company to its Entity List in more than a year, according to Axios's review of the Federal Register.
key_facts.excerpt: Commerce has not added a single company to its Entity List in more than a year, according to a review of the Federal Register, despite mounting pressure from national security officials.

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI companies are rushing to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, fearing tighter US restrictions after the Huang spy scandal.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese artificial intelligence companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centres outside China …

key_facts.fact: Beijing said the US should stop fabricating a Chinese spy narrative as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions, ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting next week.
key_facts.excerpt: Beijing says “the US should stop fabricating the so-called Chinese spy narrative as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions”; Trump and Xi meet next week

stories.headline: Foxconn posts record Q3 profit on AI servers, sees AI rack shipments growing strongly in 2027

key_facts.fact: Foxconn's Q3 2026 revenue rose 46% year on year to NT$3.02 trillion and net profit rose 34% to a record NT$77.5 billion; EPS was NT$5.51.
key_facts.excerpt: In the third quarter, Foxconn recorded revenue of NT$3.02 trillion, up 46% on-year ... net profit (attributable to owners of the parent company) of NT$77.5 billion, climbed 34% from a year ago. ... EPS for the July-September period reached NT$5.51

key_facts.fact: Net profit of T$77.5 billion (about $2.35 billion) beat the LSEG consensus of T$69.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Net profit for the July to September period for Nvidia's biggest server maker and Apple's top iPhone assembler was T$77.5 billion ($2.35 billion), up 34% on year and beating an LSEG consensus estimate of T$69.6 billion.

key_facts.fact: Foxconn predicted 'high double-digit growth' in AI rack shipments in 2027; Chairman Young Liu said cloud and networking products are already more than 50% of revenue and should exceed 60% within three to five years.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, which does not give numeric forecasts, said it predicted "high double-digit growth" in 2027 for AI rack shipments. "Cloud and networking products already account for more than 50% of our revenue this year and we expect that share to exceed 60% over the next three to five years," Chairman Young Liu said

key_facts.fact: The company raised its full-year outlook for all four major product segments and expects strong sequential and year-on-year growth in Q4, helped by shipments of a new generation of AI server racks.
key_facts.excerpt: the company has raised its outlook across all four major product segments ... with the shipment of a new generation of AI server racks, revenue from AI servers is projected to continue growing on a quarterly basis

key_facts.fact: Liu warned that chips, memory and key components are tight and that demand is expected to exceed supply next year.
key_facts.excerpt: he warned of stubborn bottlenecks in the AI and consumer electronics supply chains, with overall demand "still expected to outpace supply heading into next year".

stories.headline: China's SMIC posts record $3.19B quarter as profit more than doubles and fabs run at 97%

key_facts.fact: SMIC's Q3 2026 revenue rose 33.9% year on year (6.1% quarter on quarter) to $3.19 billion, driven by higher wafer shipments.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue was $3,190.0 million in 3Q26, an increase of 6.1% QoQ from $3,005.6 million in 2Q26. The growth was mainly due to the increase in wafer shipments in 3Q26.

key_facts.fact: Profit attributable to shareholders rose 123.4% year on year to $428.4 million, above estimates of about $396.8 million.
key_facts.excerpt: SMIC reports Q3 revenue up 34% YoY to ~$3.19B, net profit up 123% to ~$428.4M, above ~$396.8M est., and a gross margin of 29.9%, above its 26% to 28% guidance

key_facts.fact: Gross margin reached 29.9%, up from 25.3% in Q2 and 22.0% a year earlier, beating SMIC's own 26%-28% guidance, on higher utilization and product mix.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross margin was 29.9% in 3Q26, compared to 25.3% in 2Q26, due to the increase in utilization rate and the product mix change in 3Q26.

key_facts.fact: Utilization rose to 97.3% from 93.7%, and monthly capacity grew to 1,116,750 8-inch-equivalent wafers; China accounted for 90.8% of revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Monthly capacity increased to 1,116,750 standard logic 8-inch equivalent wafers in 3Q26 ... Utilization rate 97.3% ... 93.7% ... China 90.8% 90.2% 86.2%

key_facts.fact: For Q4, SMIC guides revenue up 4%-6% sequentially and gross margin of 26%-28%.
key_facts.excerpt: In the fourth quarter, the Company's revenue is expected to increase 4% to 6% sequentially, and the gross margin is expected to be in the range of 26% to 28%.

stories.headline: SoftBank leads $500M round in German humanoid maker Agile Robots at $8.5B valuation

key_facts.fact: Munich-based Agile Robots closed a $500 million Series F at an $8.5 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $2 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Munich-based Physical AI company Agile Robots has closed a Series F funding round, raising $500 million at a valuation of $8.5 billion. The round brings the company's total invested capital to $2 billion.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Group led the round, with Nvidia, Hitachi and T.Capital participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Agile Robots SE raised funds valuing the German robotics maker at $8.5 billion in a round led by SoftBank Group Corp. ... Nvidia Corp., Hitachi Ltd. and T.Capital also participated in the round.

key_facts.fact: The company builds humanoid and mobile robots, robotic arms and hands plus the AI software behind them, says it has more than 20,000 robotic systems installed, and opened a plant near Munich able to make up to 10,000 humanoids a year.
key_facts.excerpt: Agile Robots builds and deploys Physical AI – humanoid and mobile robots, robotic arms and hands, and the software and AI models behind them ... The site has the capacity to produce up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots annually.

key_facts.fact: The money will fund US expansion and more production capacity, including in Germany; Agile expects to produce about 2,000 humanoids in 2026, and its CEO said the round strengthens its position to consider an IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: The company recently opened a humanoid robot factory near Munich and expects to produce around 2,000 units in 2026. ... CEO Zhaopeng Chen also told the New York Times that the funding puts Agile in a stronger position to consider a future IPO.

key_facts.fact: A spokesman said Agile is now Europe's most valuable 'physical AI' robotics firm.
key_facts.excerpt: A spokesman told AFP that the company, founded in 2018, was now Europe's most valuable "physical AI" robotics firm.

stories.headline: CoreWeave plans $4B+ investment-grade loan at about half its junk-bond yields

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave is preparing to raise at least $4 billion through an investment-grade loan led by Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ, which could launch as early as next week and be syndicated in phases, Bloomberg reported on November 11.
key_facts.excerpt: CoreWeave Inc (NASDAQ:CRWV) is preparing to raise at least $4 billion through an investment-grade loan facility, Bloomberg reported ... led by Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc., would be syndicated in phases and could launch as early as next week

key_facts.fact: Early pricing points to a 7%-7.5% yield, roughly half that of CoreWeave's existing junk bonds.
key_facts.excerpt: Early discussions point to a yield of 7% to 7.5% on the new loan ... That works out to roughly half of what CoreWeave's junk bonds currently pay.

key_facts.fact: The financing is expected to be backed by chips and customer contracts, the structure CoreWeave used for an $8.5 billion investment-grade facility in March secured against Meta contracts.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing is expected to use chips and related contracts as backing ... In March, CoreWeave closed an $8.5 billion financing under an investment-grade facility supported by its customer agreements with Meta

key_facts.fact: The loan follows CoreWeave raising its full-year revenue outlook on November 10 to $13 billion-$13.3 billion, above the $12.9 billion consensus.
key_facts.excerpt: The specialized cloud provider raised its full-year revenue outlook on Tuesday to between $13 billion and $13.3 billion, surpassing Wall Street's $12.9 billion consensus estimate

stories.headline: IBM unveils 520-qubit Nighthawk r3 quantum chip, plans 1,040-qubit linked system in 2027

key_facts.fact: IBM announced on November 11 that its next-generation Quantum Nighthawk r3 processor will be built to accurately execute 10,000 quantum operations across 520 programmable qubits.
key_facts.excerpt: IBM (NYSE: IBM) today announced IBM Quantum Nighthawk r3, its next-generation processor, will be built to accurately execute 10,000 quantum operations across 520 qubits

key_facts.fact: The chip has 2,034 total physical qubits and adds 10 chip-to-chip interconnects ('l-couplers'); IBM plans to link two r3 processors into a single 1,040-qubit system in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The new processor is designed to support 10,000 quantum operations on 520 programmable qubits, with 2,034 total physical qubits. ... introducing 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers ... In 2027, IBM plans to connect two Nighthawk r3 processors into a single 1,040-qubit system

key_facts.fact: Clients and partners including E.ON, Algorithmiq and Q-CTRL have run more than 34 billion circuits on the current Nighthawk r2, reporting speedups of up to 19x over previous IBM processors.
key_facts.excerpt: Clients and partners including E.ON, Algorithmiq, and Q-CTRL have run more than 34 billion circuits on Nighthawk r2, reporting speedups of up to 19x beyond previous IBM quantum processors

key_facts.fact: IBM presented the chip at its annual Quantum Developer Conference; it is not its first 1,000-plus-qubit chip (Condor had 1,121), but Nighthawk is designed for high precision and speed.
key_facts.excerpt: Auf seiner jährlichen Quantum Developer Conference präsentierte IBM am Mittwoch ... Schon IBMs Condor stellte 1121 Qubits bereit. Anders als dieser sollen die Nighthawk-Chips aber Rechnungen mit einer hohen Präzision und Geschwindigkeit ausführen können.
